$comment: The contract between the bundling pipeline and the Rust shell.
WRITER: app/scripts/build-sidecar.mjs. READERS: app/src-tauri/src/paths.rs and
app/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json, whose bundle.externalBin and bundle.resources must match
'externalBin' and 'bundleResources' below word for word.
Nothing else may hardcode these names. If you are about to write a path literal in
main.rs, read it from here instead.
Background: docs/TRAY-DESIGN.md section 2 (Packaging a Node core as a sidecar binary)
and section 5 (Repo shape and release).
$coreBundleIsEsm: core.mjs, NOT core.cjs. TRAY-DESIGN says core.cjs and TRAY-DESIGN is wrong about the
extension, for a reason nobody could have known before trying it: src/cli.ts ends in a
top level await, and esbuild refuses that outright with the cjs output format. It is a
build error, not a preference. Node decides a file's module system by extension and an
.cjs file containing ESM is a syntax error, so the name has to follow the format.
Everything that names this file reads it from here.

$comment: Owned by app/src-tauri/src/paths.rs (env_names). Repeated here so the two sides
cannot drift. The build script takes --node instead of an env var on purpose, so a
build time override can never be confused with the runtime one.
The sidecar IS node.exe, renamed. So the first argument to the child is the core
bundle, which the shell must pass as an ABSOLUTE path resolved from the resource dir.
watchArgs is the literal argument vector with the two placeholders substituted.
-c comes after the subcommand on purpose: watch declares its own -c and configOf() in
src/commands/index.ts accepts it on either side.
$m4Args: M4. setup is the same machine channel the watch command has had since M1, and it is
what the first run window spawns: one JSON line per event on stdout, human prose on
stderr, and one payload-carrying stdin form. docs/ASK-PROTOCOL.md is the contract.
doctor takes -c as of M4, alongside --json. It used to take neither, on the grounds
that it checks the setup the wizard made in the folder the wizard owns; the wizard makes
one wherever -c says, and a tray running against an override has to ask about the setup
it is really using. Without it the health window on a development machine or under the
rig would report on the machine's real ~/.photo-pigeon, which the safety rules forbid.
--json is a passthrough of the DoctorReport that src/wizard/doctor.ts has always
produced, past the layer that flattened it for a terminal.
$foldersArgs: Editing the watched folder list from the status window. One request, one JSON
line on stdout, human prose on stderr: the shape doctor --json already has, and
not the ndjson stream watch and setup use, because there is no run here to
narrate and no stopped event to end it with. src/commands/folders.ts is the
contract and it answers every request, including the ones that change nothing.
{foldersAction} is add or remove. {folderPath} is a string the page received
from ipc::pick_folder or out of the core's own started event, handed straight
back for the core to validate exactly as it validates a path a terminal user
typed. The shell never reads it and never writes it.
$m3Words: The four words M3 added to the core's stdin vocabulary, plus the event that
confirms the one of them that matters most. paths.rs already carries these exact
strings as serde defaults, so naming them here changes no behaviour today; it
makes them renameable from one file tomorrow, and it gives app/e2e/run-m3.ps1 a
contract to read that a Rust drift test holds the shell to.
detach is NOT stop: see docs/TRAY-DESIGN.md section 2, the detach protocol.

$comment: Start with Windows, M3. WRITER: app/src-tauri/src/autostart.rs, which drives
auto-launch 0.5 directly rather than tauri-plugin-autostart, because the plugin
physically cannot write a quoted value. READER: app/e2e/run-m3.ps1, which prefers
this block over its own m3-vocabulary.json fallback.
runValueName MUST equal tauri.conf.json productName: the generated installer.nsi
uninstalls with DeleteRegValue HKCU "...\Run" "${PRODUCTNAME}", so a value under
any other name outlives the uninstall forever.
The value DATA is quoted and the flag sits outside the closing quote:
"C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Photo Pigeon\photo-pigeon.exe" --autostart
The install directory contains a space on every machine now, so the quoting is
load bearing rather than prudent. Background: docs/TRAY-DESIGN.md sections 4 and 6.
How the shell finds the core bundle at runtime, dev and installed.
On Windows tauri_utils::platform::resource_dir_from returns the exe directory
unconditionally (platform.rs, the `if cfg!(target_os = "windows") || ...` branch), so
resource_dir() and the exe dir are the same directory in BOTH cases and one join
covers both. tauri-build's build.rs copies bundle.resources into the cargo target dir
keeping the relative path (tauri_utils::resources::resource_relpath), and copies
externalBin next to the exe with the target triple suffix stripped and the directory
dropped. The NSIS bundler lays the install directory out the same way.
order: 1. PHOTO_PIGEON_CORE_JS set and non empty: use it verbatim, skip everything else.
This is the seam that lets a test, or a dev iterating on the core, point the tray
at ../../dist/cli.js without a rebuild. Node runs the unbundled ESM CLI exactly as
well as it runs the bundle.
This also matches under tauri dev, because tauri-build stages both into the cargo
target dir, so dev exercises the shipped shape rather than a second one.
